extracted.intended_audience: organisations and consortia (universities, research institutions, businesses, SMEs and other non-academic organisations) considering applying to MSCA Staff Exchanges under Horizon Europe
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility rules for preparing and submitting a proposal to the Marie Skłodowska‑Curie Actions (MSCA) Staff Exchanges action, covering consortium composition, eligible staff, duration, allowed costs and submission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of Staff Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: The Staff Exchanges action funds short-term international and inter-sectoral exchanges of staff members involved in research and innovation activities of participating organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to develop sustainable collaborative projects between different organisations from the academic and non-academic sectors (in particular SMEs), based in Europe and beyond. Exchanged staff benefit from new knowledge, skills and career development perspectives, while participating organisations increase their research and innovation capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium eligibility (who can apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff Exchanges are open to international consortia of universities, research institutions, businesses, SMEs and other non-academic organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are made on behalf of an organisation or consortium. Individual staff members are selected by their sending organisations to take part in the planned exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum consortium size and country distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The consortium must include at least three organisations in three different countries, two of which need to be located in a different EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Above this minimum, the participation of organisations from any country is possible. Participation of organisations from non-associated third countries is strongly encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectoral balance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The consortium must include participating organisations from both academic and non-academic sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is particular emphasis on inter-sectoral collaborations, especially involvement of SMEs, to foster knowledge exchange between academia and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration and secondment length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff Exchanges projects can last up to four years. The grant funds the mobility of seconded staff members from one month to one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondments must fit within the 1-month to 1-year per mobility window and the overall project must not exceed four years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reintegration / return expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff involved should return to their sending organisations after the secondment, to ensure long-term impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return to the sending organisation is expected so that seconded staff can pass on their knowledge and foster sustained collaboration and career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible seconded staff roles and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff funded by Staff Exchanges can be researchers at any career stage, from PhD candidates to postdoctoral researchers, as well as administrative, technical or managerial staff involved in research and innovation activities; they can be of any nationality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility covers a broad range of personnel involved in R&I activities, not only researchers; nationality is not a restricting factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances and eligible costs covered by the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Seconded staff receives a top-up allowance (for travel, accommodation, subsistence costs), which is on top of the salary paid by their organisation, and a special needs allowance, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition, funding is provided for research, training and networking activities, and for management and indirect costs. The top-up is intended to cover mobility-related costs while salary remains with the sending organisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission process and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to MSCA Staff Exchanges can be submitted at any time from the opening date of the chosen call. The completed proposal, including all annexes, should be submitted by the specified submission deadline of the chosen call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should use the EU Funding & Tenders Portal to find calls, partners and submit proposals. All relevant documents are available on the dedicated call page (MSCA work programme, general annexes, guide for applicants, specific FAQs, application and evaluation forms, online manual on how to submit an application). For further guidance consult the MSCA 'how to apply' page and the European Research Executive Agency website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility for selecting individual participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual staff members are selected by their sending organisations to take part in the planned exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and nomination of secondees is the sending organisation's responsibility; the grant funds the mobility and allowances but the sending organisation retains employment and salary arrangements.
